answer: Second-order proximity is typically measured as the similarity between the vertices' neighborhood distributions, i.e., how similar their in-neighbor sets and out-neighbor sets are (for example, via a dot product, cosine, or Jaccard-style overlap of their neighborhood vectors). If two vertices share no common in-neighbors or out-neighbors, their neighborhood overlap is empty, so the second-order proximity is set to 0.
